draw.text: 1. Two sentences, chopped into tokens. [CLS] goes first, [SEP] separates them

steps.say: Start at the bottom left. Two sentences are split into tokens, with a special CLS token at the front and a SEP token between them. Some words are hidden behind a mask.

draw.text: 2. Every token becomes a vector, and the BERT layers let all tokens look at each other

steps.say: Each token becomes an embedding, the yellow boxes. The blue BERT layers then let every word look at every other word, in both directions, so the model builds up context.

draw.text: 3. Pre-training games: guess the masked words (Mask LM), and guess whether B really follows A (NSP, read from C)

steps.say: The red arrows are the two pre-training games. Mask LM guesses the hidden words. NSP uses the C output to guess whether sentence B really comes after sentence A.

draw.text: 4. Copy all the learned weights into each task model

steps.say: The dotted arrows mean you copy those learned weights into a fresh copy of BERT for each task, like MNLI, NER or SQuAD. The cards are stacked to show there are many of these copies.

draw.text: 5. Feed in the task's own input, add a tiny output layer, and fine-tune everything. Here it's question + paragraph, predicting the answer's start and end

steps.say: For SQuAD, the input becomes a question plus a paragraph, and a small output layer points to where the answer starts and ends. The takeaway is that it's the same body every time: pre-train once, then fine-tune cheaply for each task.
